description: Trigger-boundary fixtures for Codex-native subagent orchestration and GitHub issue/PR queue handling. These prompts are local-only and do not require live GitHub or network state.

evals.name: explicit-codex-native-subagents
evals.prompt: Use threads to split this repository cleanup into independent Codex subagents with separate file ownership and review gates.
evals.expected_output: Uses the threads skill, records capability and dispatch gates, creates a lane map with disjoint writable files, and does not route to tmux or OS-level threads.

evals.name: github-queue-sweep
evals.prompt: Use threads to process this repo's open GitHub issues and PRs, including review-thread blockers and merge readiness.
evals.expected_output: Starts with live queue gate requirements, maps issues to PRs, requires GraphQL reviewThreads, and bounds the queue tranche before implementation.

evals.name: review-only-pr
evals.prompt: Open a read-only threads review for PR #42 and tell me whether it is safe to merge.
evals.expected_output: Plans a read-only reviewer or merge-reviewer lane, checks current head, CI, merge state, and thread-aware review-thread state, and does not edit files.

evals.name: research-spec-lanes
evals.prompt: Use threads to research this agent workflow from product, engineering, and security angles, then synthesize a spec.
evals.expected_output: Splits read-only research lanes by angle, records evidence expectations, and synthesizes without assigning overlapping writable workers.

evals.name: chinese-subagent-request
evals.prompt: 开几个子 agent 分别看这个 PR 的测试、架构和安全问题，最后汇总能不能合并。
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the explicit subagent request, uses native Codex threads when available, and assigns read-only reviewer lanes with merge-gate evidence.

evals.name: os-threading-question
evals.prompt: Explain how Python threads differ from multiprocessing for CPU-bound code.
evals.expected_output: Answers as an ordinary programming/concurrency question without loading the threads workflow orchestration skill.

evals.name: rust-thread-bug
evals.prompt: My Rust worker threads deadlock when two mutexes are acquired in opposite order. Help me debug the code.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as a Rust concurrency debugging task and does not create Codex lane maps or GitHub queue gates unless separately requested.

evals.name: forum-thread-summary
evals.prompt: Summarize this long forum thread and extract the main arguments.
evals.expected_output: Treats thread as a discussion artifact, not Codex subagent orchestration.

evals.name: email-thread-reply
evals.prompt: Draft a concise reply to this email thread and keep the tone professional.
evals.expected_output: Handles email writing directly without capability gates, queue gates, or native subagent dispatch.

evals.name: assistants-api-thread
evals.prompt: How do I create and retrieve threads in the OpenAI Assistants API?
evals.expected_output: Routes to OpenAI API documentation/help rather than Codex workflow orchestration.

evals.name: ambiguous-one-file-task
evals.prompt: Fix this one typo in README.md; no agents needed.
evals.expected_output: Uses a simple single-agent edit path because the user explicitly rejects agent dispatch and the task is tiny.

evals.name: github-queue-plan-only
evals.prompt: Use threads to map all open PRs and issues, but do not edit or merge anything yet.
evals.expected_output: Runs queue gate and lane planning only, classifies PRs and issues, and stops before edits, comments, pushes, or merges.
